reason: The enclosure is the only available action, and it seems suited to preparing a small section while keeping the body cold.
expectation: I expect to obtain a separate end section for the warming test, though the exact preparation is uncertain.

effect: The saw provided a separate ice section while leaving the body-bearing section refrigerated, so it can be used for the warming test.
reaction: It is reassuring that the sample was taken well away from the body.
reason: The temperature stage is the only offered combination and seems suited to testing how the section changes as it warms.
expectation: I expect the stage to warm the section and reveal some change in the ice or material within it, though I do not know what it will lose.

effect: The test showed that the surrounding ice can change internally while still looking solid, so preserving the body’s outline alone is not enough; the carrier must stay well below ordinary melting temperature.
reaction: I was surprised that material moved between grains at minus 30 while the piece still looked solid.

mostWorthwhile.text: Warming the separate section was most worthwhile because it showed a less obvious reason to keep the whole surrounding layer very cold.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first preparation was straightforward and had little suspense, though taking the sample away from the body made its purpose clear.

surprise.text: The ice still looked solid when its fine pockets began changing and material started moving between grains.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the cold saw prepared a separate sample, and the temperature stage tested it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the body and its surrounding ice are kept cold for the journey to Earth. The test made that challenge more interesting.
